## About this example
A laboratory arch of 16 voussoirs, traced over its own photograph with the
**three-point** tool: three clicks on the intrados and three on the extrados fix
two circles exactly, which is what a ring photographed square to the camera
asks for.

*What it exercises.* Image import and calibration; the kg-cm unit system, so
every force on screen is a kilogram-force and not a pixel; one **applied point
load** hung on the haunch; both ends of the line **imposed** at the springings
by the classical trial-pole construction; the force polygon lettered after Bow,
so a stone can be followed from the arch to the polygon by eye; and the three
sliders that move within the admissible family.

*Try.* Drag the thrust slider and watch the line pivot while the reactions
follow. Move the load along the arch and see which joints go critical first.
